findings.title: Unvalidated nb_blocks allows heap out-of-bounds in argon2i_32
findings.evidence: argon2i_32() passes caller-supplied nb_blocks straight into config.nb_blocks (line 328) with no minimum check; _validate_u32 (lines 316-319) is only applied to the buffer lengths, not to nb_blocks or nb_iterations. The work area is sized malloc(nb_blocks*1024) (line 345) and then handed to crypto_argon2 (line 347). In monocypher.c, crypto_argon2 computes segment_size = nb_blocks/nb_lanes/4 and lane_size = segment_size*4 (lines 752-753); with nb_lanes forced to 1 (line 330 of the .pyx), any nb_blocks < 4 makes segment_size = lane_size = 0. The core then unconditionally fills two 1024-byte blocks per lane, writing blocks[0] and blocks[1] (monocypher.c line 781), so nb_blocks of 0 or 1 writes up to 2048 bytes past a work_area of nb_blocks*1024 bytes (heap buffer overflow). For nb_blocks in {0,1,2,3} it additionally computes last_block = blocks + lane_size - 1 = blocks - 1 (monocypher.c line 902) and reads 1024 bytes before the allocation at line 911. The public header documents the required precondition nb_blocks >= 8 * nb_lanes (monocypher.h line 160). An attacker who controls the Argon2 cost parameters (e.g. KDF parameters parsed from untrusted input or a password-hash string) calls argon2i_32(nb_blocks=1, ...) and triggers heap memory corruption/out-of-bounds read.
